correctness.rationale: The fixed metric is the unit-edge star metric and the finite Markov generator has symmetric rates. Kantorovich duality reduces the global W1 coefficient to the infinity norm of the gradient heat operator. The exact gradient ODE, its two eigenvalues and row coefficients are derived in RESULT.md. In both sign cases for the fast-row offdiagonal coefficient, the slow row is no smaller, using Delta<=r+1 and lambda_minus<=1. The slow-edge potential gives equality, so the result holds for all times and rates. A unique derivative zero gives the exact peak; explicit expansions give the logarithmic small-rate law. The packaged independent vertex-generator checker passed 693 numerical assertions. These tests are not used as an infinite proof; the conclusion does not extend beyond the stated graph and parameter ranges.

value.rationale: The exact all-time transport coefficient and globally maximizing Dirac pair are nontrivial for an inhomogeneous, nonnormal gradient semigroup on a branching graph: ordinary-edge gradient coefficients change sign with time. The work quantifies metastable transport buildup under one conductance defect, determines a global peak at all positive rates, and derives an explicit logarithmic weak-rate correction and peak-time scale. The one-defect star is a natural finite comparison model for kinetic rates decoupled from geometric distance. The all-rate slow-edge optimality is not supplied by the equal-rate star or path-bottleneck formulas.
